slides.title: US market entry: should Onsoo enter in 2027, and by which route?

paragraphs.text: US market entry: should Onsoo enter in 2027, and by which route?
Recommendation to CEO Park Ji-won and the Board of Onsoo Botanicals for the March 2027 board meeting
Prepared November 2026 from the planning team's briefing pack only (no external research)
All company, competitor and market figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data. $ = US dollars; M = millions

slides.title: Executive summary: enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A), reset the 2030 targets, and add specialty retail only after awareness reaches 20%

paragraphs.text: Executive summary: enter the US in 2027 through Amazon (Option A), reset the 2030 targets, and add specialty retail only after awareness reaches 20%
The US is the right market for the 2027 slot

US K-beauty facial skincare is $3.6B and grew 17% a year in 2021–25. The Amazon pilot nearly doubled monthly units in six months at 4.5 stars. By 2030, Option A builds a US business of $26M, against $7M of extra revenue from a Japan scale-up. Japan is safer on cash to 2030, and it can follow in 2028.
Amazon-led (A) beats retail-led (B) on every board test

On its own inputs, B breaches the $18M cash cap (–$20.8M by 2030), does not pay back and cuts group margin to 4.5% in 2027. Its 4.5 units/door/week is what brands with >20% awareness sell (Onsoo: 4%), and its 1.3× Amazon halo rests on a correlation.
Even Option A will not hit every target, so the board should reset two of them

A's peak cash need is $1.9–4.9M in every case except the severe one, and group margin stays at 9% or more. But payback by 2030 needs ad cost (ACoS) of ≤28.6% against a 32% benchmark (otherwise ~2032), and 2030 revenue is $26M, not $40M ($40M around 2032).
Specialty retail should come later, behind stricter gates

At the CEO's 15% awareness trigger, brands sell a median 3.5 units/door/week, below the retailer's 4.0 removal line. Adding national retail in 2029 would cut 2029 group margin to 6.8% and leave US cash at –$9.6M in 2030. Gate retail on ≥20% awareness and a measured halo.
(1) Approve Option A with a $5M peak-cash envelope.   (2) Restate the US targets: $25M+ revenue in 2030, $40M by ~2032, payback by 2030 at ≤28.6% ACoS and by 2032 at most.
(3) Reject retail-first and replace the 2029 retail trigger with evidence gates.   (4) Review the Japan scale-up for 2028; the bandwidth limit applies to 2027 only.
Source: Onsoo planning-team briefing pack (Nov 2026); team analysis. Detailed calculations in the appendix.

slides.title: We tested the CEO's hypothesis against five conditions. Two hold, one holds in part and two fail, so the route stands but the targets and retail trigger change

paragraphs.text: We tested the CEO's hypothesis against five conditions. Two hold, one holds in part and two fail, so the route stands but the targets and retail trigger change
Starting hypothesis (CEO): “Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%.”
What would have to be true
1  The US is a better use of 2027 than a Japan scale-up

US K-beauty is growing 17% a year against 1.5% for Japanese skincare. Option A reaches $26M by 2030, against $7M for Japan. But Japan is ahead on cash to 2030 unless ACoS stays at or below the pilot's 28%.
2  Amazon is the right lead channel
Amazon carries 41% of US K-beauty sales; 61% of K-beauty buyers buy there most often. The pilot sells at 4.5 stars; repeat is 29% against a 31% benchmark.
3  Amazon-led stays within the cash, payback and margin limits
Peak cash is $1.9–3.2M against the $18M cap, and group margin stays at 9.1% or more. Payback by 2030 holds only at ACoS ≤28.6%; at the 32% scaling benchmark it slips to ~2032.
4  It puts Onsoo on the way to $40M by 2030
Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030, and Option B $37.6M (while breaking the cash cap). At 20% growth after 2030, Option A reaches $40M in about 2032.
5  Retail added in 2029 at >$10M Amazon sales and >15% awareness pays off
At 10–20% awareness, brands sell a median 3.5 units/door/week, below the 4.0 removal line. A national add in 2029 takes 2029 group margin to 6.8% and US cash to –$9.6M by 2030.
Revised answer: keep the Amazon-led route; restate the 2030 revenue and payback targets around ad cost; replace the 15% retail trigger with a 20% awareness gate plus a measured halo.
Source: Briefing pack §4 (CEO hypothesis), Tables 1–9, §10–12; team analysis.

slides.title: By 2030 a US launch builds a business nearly 4× the size of a Japan scale-up; Japan is safer on cash and can follow in 2028

paragraphs.text: By 2030 a US launch builds a business nearly 4× the size of a Japan scale-up; Japan is safer on cash and can follow in 2028

Why the US anyway: the board's ambition is a US business, and only the US offers a market growing 11× faster than Japan's. By 2030 Option A is still growing 29% a year, while J's additions are levelling off.
What Japan offers: about $4M more cash by 2030 if US ad costs reach the benchmark. The bandwidth limit covers 2027 only, so a Japan scale-up can be reviewed for 2028 rather than given up.

slides.title: Option B assumes the sell-through of brands with >20% awareness; at Onsoo's 4%, the median brand falls below the 4.0 removal line

paragraphs.text: Option B assumes the sell-through of brands with >20% awareness; at Onsoo's 4%, the median brand falls below the 4.0 removal line
First-year sell-through by aided awareness among category buyers, units per door per week
Onsoo sits in the lowest tier
Aided awareness is 4% of US skincare buyers (9% among K-beauty buyers). Both are below 10%
At the tier median of 2.6, 600 doors sell ~81k units a year, not 140k. Even the top quartile (3.4) is below 4.0, so the most likely result is removal after 12 months
It comes from the retailer's own deck on successful newcomers, a survivor sample, and matches the >20% tier. The independent analytics data covers 46 brands
Clearing 4.0 with confidence needs >20% awareness: that tier's lower quartile is 3.9
Source: Table 8 (retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 newcomer brands; leading retailer removes brands below 4.0 units/door/week at the 12-month review); §10 survey (Sep 2026, n=1,200); Table 5.

slides.title: The 1.3× retail halo is unproven: the 0.71 correlation fits Amazon success leading to retail doors just as well as the reverse

paragraphs.text: The 1.3× retail halo is unproven: the 0.71 correlation fits Amazon success leading to retail doors just as well as the reverse
US K-beauty buyers shop and discover away from the shelf
Retailers add doors for brands that already sell. Higher Amazon sales and more doors move together whichever causes which
Saebom shows the order: Amazon-first in 2022, about $30M US revenue by 2025, and only then 300 retail doors
The memo gives no before/after or test-vs-control evidence, so 1.3× is an assumption, not a measurement
Mooncrest, retail-first in 450 doors (2023): removed from shelves in 2025, with an estimated cumulative US loss of $21M
Amazon-first: one of three entrants reached about $30M; two are below $5M. Amazon-first is not safe either, which is why section 4 adds stop gates
61% of K-beauty buyers buy K-beauty on Amazon most often; 22% at specialty retail
38% found their last new brand on TikTok; 17% in a store
52% cite price compared with US brands. The $28 retail shelf price is 17% above Amazon's $24

What the halo would have to be for retail to pay for itself: 600 doors at 4.6 units/week earn $1.08M against $7.5M of retail fixed costs. Covering the $6.4M gap at $4.73 a unit takes 1.36M extra Amazon units a year.
That means Amazon sales 2.2–2.6× Option A's (2030 / 2029), not 1.3×. The halo would need to be several times larger than even the unproven figure.
Implication: the case for retail-first rests on a sell-through rate and a halo that the evidence does not support. Amazon first, with retail earned later, is the sequence the evidence backs.
Source: §12 (board member memo, 30 brands); Table 9 (recent K-beauty US entrants); §10 survey; Table 4; team analysis.

slides.title: Ad cost decides payback: Option A recovers its cash by 2030 only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%, roughly the pilot's level

paragraphs.text: Ad cost decides payback: Option A recovers its cash by 2030 only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%, roughly the pilot's level
Option A cumulative cash at end-2030 by ACoS, $M
28.6% at today's duty; 26.9% if the duty rises to 25% in mid-2027
Each +1 pt of ACoS costs $0.67M of cumulative cash by 2030
The 25% plan figure runs against the evidence

The planning team assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures. The agency data says the opposite: brands scaling from $5M to $20M on Amazon run a median 32% (range 26–38%), because cost per click rises on broader keywords
Option A scales from $7M to $26M, squarely in that range. The pilot's 28% was on a small budget
Source: Team model (Option A volumes and costs per Tables 4–6); pilot ACoS (§6); agency benchmark (§11); tariff review (§13).

slides.title: Even in a severe downside, Option A's peak cash need stays below $8M and group margin above 8%: the risk is to payback timing, not the balance sheet

paragraphs.text: Even in a severe downside, Option A's peak cash need stays below $8M and group margin above 8%: the risk is to payback timing, not the balance sheet
What this means for the board
Affordability is not the issue. Peak cash is 11–44% of the $18M cap and group margin stays at 8.8% or more in every case
Payback is the issue. It holds only in the two cases where ACoS is at or below the pilot's level
The severe case must be stopped, not funded. At 38% ACoS and 25% duty each unit earns $1.26, so 825k units in 2030 cannot cover $2.1M of fixed costs. Hence the stop rules in section 4
Upside not modelled: a weaker won (10% ≈ +$0.37 a unit, ≈ +$1.0M to 2030)
Source: Team model. *Payback after 2030 extrapolates Option A at 10–20% annual unit growth after 2030 (team assumption; not in the briefing pack).

slides.title: No route reaches $40M of US revenue in 2030 within the limits; on the Amazon path, $40M comes around 2032 if growth holds at 20% a year

paragraphs.text: No route reaches $40M of US revenue in 2030 within the limits; on the Amazon path, $40M comes around 2032 if growth holds at 20% a year
The gap is in the plans themselves
Option B plan: $37.6M, and $40.9M only if retail is counted at shelf price rather than Onsoo's wholesale price. It gets there by breaking the cash cap
$25M+ US revenue in 2030, $40M by ~2032, both conditional on hitting the 2028 gate. This keeps “on the way to $40M” honest
Precedent: Saebom reached ~$30M about three years after an Amazon-first entry
Source: Tables 4–5; team model. 2031–33 values are team extrapolations of Option A at 10% and 20% annual unit growth (not in the briefing pack).

slides.title: Retail should wait for ≥20% awareness and a measured halo: the CEO's 15% trigger falls in the tier whose median sits below the 4.0 removal line

paragraphs.text: Retail should wait for ≥20% awareness and a measured halo: the CEO's 15% trigger falls in the tier whose median sits below the 4.0 removal line
CEO plan as written: Option A + 600 doors in 2029
≥20% aided awareness among all US facial-skincare buyers, the base Table 8 uses
At 10–20% the median is 3.5 units/door/week (IQR 2.8–4.3), below 4.0. The >20% tier's median is 4.6
>$10M and ACoS ≤30% and cumulative US cash on track to turn positive
Retail's $7.5M a year has to be carried by a profitable Amazon business
cumulative US cash at end-2030, against +$2.4M for Amazon-only, even granting 4.6 units/door/week and the 1.3× halo
Regional door test: measure Amazon uplift in test regions against control regions
Retail pays for itself only with a 2.2–2.6× halo; the 0.71 correlation shows neither the size nor the direction
Not before 2030; a test-sized programme first, then a separate board investment case
A 2029 national add breaks the 2029 margin floor and the 2030 payback (right)
group operating margin in 2029, below the 8% floor

Implication: treat specialty retail as an awareness investment that Amazon performance has to earn, not as a 2029 calendar commitment. The gates make the decision depend on evidence the board can see.
yearly contribution per door at 4.6 units/week, against $12,500 per door of retail fixed costs
Source: Table 8; §10 survey; Tables 4–6; team model of the CEO plan (Option A, plus 600 doors from 2029 at 4.6 units/door/week, 1.3× Amazon halo, $7.5M a year of retail fixed costs).

slides.title: A stage-gated 2027–30 plan lets the board stop with about $2.5M at risk if the early signals disappoint

paragraphs.text: A stage-gated 2027–30 plan lets the board stop with about $2.5M at risk if the early signals disappoint
Set up the US entity; MoCRA registration; US-English labels
Take over the Amazon listings from the cross-border seller
Launch four more SKUs (seven in total)
$0.7M off-Amazon marketing, TikTok first (38% discover there)
Miss two or more: cut to a hold mode with low fixed cost; ~$2.0–2.5M spent
Re-run the awareness survey on the Table 8 base
If awareness ≥15%, design a regional retail test
Aided awareness ≥20% and a measured halo from the test
National retail only through a separate board investment case
Tariff decision (mid-2027): at 25% duty, breakeven ACoS falls to 26.9%; re-plan price and cost if it passes
ACoS is tracked monthly against the 28.6% breakeven, not the 25% plan

Source: Team recommendation. Gate thresholds are set from the pilot (§6), the agency ACoS benchmark (§11), the repeat benchmark (§6) and Table 8. Cash at risk = cumulative cash at end-2027 (–$1.9M at plan, –$2.4M at 32% ACoS).

slides.title: We ask the board to approve four decisions in March 2027

paragraphs.text: We ask the board to approve four decisions in March 2027
Approve US entry in 2027 through the Amazon-led route (Option A)
With a US peak-cash envelope of $5M, covering the downside case (–$4.9M) and well inside the $18M cap. Any request beyond $5M comes back to the board.
Restate the US targets to match the evidence
US revenue of $25M+ in 2030 and $40M by ~2032. Payback by end-2030 if ACoS ≤28.6%; the board accepts slippage to no later than 2032 provided peak cash stays inside the envelope.
Reject the retail-first route (Option B) and replace the 2029 retail trigger
Specialty retail only with ≥20% aided awareness among all skincare buyers, a measured halo from a regional test and a separate investment case, and not before 2030.
Keep Japan as the next launch, not the alternative
Ask the Head of Japan to bring the Japan scale-up (+$7M revenue by 2030, +$1.8M cumulative cash) to the 2028 plan, subject to US Gate 1.
Source: Team recommendation based on the analysis in this document.

slides.title: Choices we made where the briefing pack was silent or ambiguous

paragraphs.text: Choices we made where the briefing pack was silent or ambiguous
Read as $40M of US revenue in calendar 2030, the stricter reading. Under a looser reading (“on a path to $40M”), Option A's 2032 trajectory could qualify.
Amazon revenue at the $24 consumer price (Onsoo sells directly via FBA); retail revenue at the $14 wholesale price Onsoo receives.

Contribution – annual fixed costs – one-time costs – increase in inventory. Inventory = 4 months of landed cost (ex-factory + freight + duty) of each year's units, not released by 2030. No tax, interest or FX change.
(Ex-US plan revenue × 11.0% + US operating result) ÷ (ex-US + US revenue). One-time costs and fixtures expensed (conservative); inventory excluded from the P&L.
As in the planning team's forecast, doors are counted as selling for the full year from 2027; new doors in 2029–30 carry $1,100 of fixtures each.
No working-capital data was provided, so none is modelled. J figures are incremental to the existing Japan business.
Read as applying to 2027 launches only, so a Japan scale-up can be considered for 2028.
Extrapolations at 10% and 20% annual unit growth are team assumptions, used only for payback year and $40M timing.
Applied to all SKUs, following the planning team. Real SKU-mix margins may differ (the hero is 31% of group revenue).
Source: Team notes. Questions could not be put to the planning team during the work, so each choice above is the option we recommend. They are listed so the board can challenge them.

Payback at risk; benchmark case shown
